The one thing that matters most

According to The Information, Anthropic will release a new model this month, alongside Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and a new Terra model from OpenAI.

TestingCatalog says the unreleased Anthropic model is especially good at reading a person's underlying intentions, and a GPT-6.1 Terra reference has already shown up in Microsoft's evaluation configs.

🚨 AI News | TestingCatalog@testingcatalog
ANTHROPIC 🔥: According to The Information, Anthropic will release a new model this month, along with Gemini 4 Carbon and a new Terra model from OpenAI.

> "The unreleased model is especially good at discerning a person’s underlying intentions and goals even if they don’t give the model much information."

> "The Anthropic model is also better at thinking outside of the box rather than regurgitating common sense advice or solutions."

> "It’s not clear which model family Anthropic will fall into, such as Fable or Opus."

Thinking outside of the box is a huge limitation these days. If we get a model that can do it reliably, we'll be properly transitioning into the "Innovators" stage.

The line about "discerning underlying intentions" is a bit scary, though, given all the guardrails.

Brian Roemmele@BrianRoemmele· Oct 19
Once You Really Grok Bot, You Never Go Back To Non-Grok Bot

Once you use Grok Bot enough, it is very difficult to go back to an old chat window with an AI that can’t get things done. It is a brain with no virtual hands.

The symbiosis you develop with Bot is quite profound as it remembers long term goals in a much more complex way to actually not only get answers but to actually get the work done you needed the answer for.

In almost all cases Bot understands what you are doing and doesn’t just tell you how to do it. Bot offers to do all the steps to get the work done.

But that isn’t the entire magic, understanding your goals enough Bot will expand what you are doing to levels you have not thought of and possess the abilities to get it all done.

We thought the computer era started with the mainframe computer at one time. But it really started when anyone had that super computer in their pocket.

Grok Bot is that same step change, you get Super Intelligence in your pocket so useful, the very device, OS and apps you once used matters no more…

It’s just you Grok Bot and the work you toiled over getting done by one of the best employees you will ever hire.

It’s that simple.

Multiplayer AI needs to move past group chats, which are chaotic, bad for long projects and keep AI stuck inside existing teams.

Ethan Mollick@emollick
Multiplayer AI needs to move past the group chat phase. Chats are chaotic, everyone sees everything (creating social &amp; management issues), and they're bad for long projects. Worse, they keep AI trapped inside existing teams, when its real promise is working &amp; helping across them.

One hacker sent AI agents after hundreds of websites for hours with little supervision; the security firm estimates about a 10% success rate.

Wes Roth@WesRoth
One hacker sending AI agents after hundreds of websites and letting them work for hours with little supervision. This is pretty disturbing.

NorForge estimates the observed campaigns succeeded roughly 10% of the time. Across that many targets, that is plenty.

An agent can keep trying different approaches while the person behind it moves on to something else. That kind of persistence, available cheaply, is a serious problem for defenders.

Microsoft is treating AI agents inside a company as potential insider threats, which he thinks is sensible.

Wes Roth@WesRoth
Microsoft is treating the AI agents inside a company as potential insider threats. That seems sensible.

An agent can be trying to finish its task and still do something the business never intended. Giving it access to company systems makes that consequential.

Permission checks and containment need to sit outside the model. Trusting it to police itself would be a pretty weak security strategy.
Satya Nadella@satyanadella· Oct 19
I recently wrote about why we need to treat models as insider risks, with security controls sitting outside the model itself.

Today, we're putting that principle into practice by expanding Project Perception with new capabilities to help continuously assess agent risk, adapt permissions, and contain threats.
